answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to climb a personal summit of sequential memory-hard proofs, each bound to its own public key and the latest network hash. The terrace of working memory needed cannot be shared; a farm running many clones on one machine sees thrashing that multiplies runtime superlinearly. Each fake must also post an ivory-colored unique collateral token that is slashed if its proof path diverges from honest timing. Attacker cost thus grows with headcount and cannot be amortized.
